_note: The culture pack (engine/cgi/acting/culture.py): display rules, how a feeling is shown and by whom, played into every acting sheet. A rule changes only what a hand-written beat leaves to the draft. `python -m engine cgi culture --chapter 1` shows what each rule changes. A draft until the owner approves it.

rules.name: a child shows joy and wonder openly
rules.why: Open positive feeling is allowed in children (Matsumoto 1990, 2008); anime plays it in full: the mouth and brows move.

rules.name: elders hold grief in
rules.why: Gaman: Japanese display rules play sadness down more than almost anywhere, most of all for elders (Matsumoto et al. 2008). The eyes carry it; the face stays still.

rules.name: distress is played down before a child
rules.why: Adults mask distress in front of children (in-group display rules, Matsumoto 1990).

rules.name: anger is held in
rules.why: Anger is the feeling Japanese display rules mask most (Matsumoto 1990).

rules.name: ma after a strong feeling
rules.why: Ma: the pause that lets a feeling land. Anime holds the key pose instead of moving on.
